title: Phrasal Verbs in High Finance
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Estos 'phrasal verbs' financieros de alto nivel son indispensables en el mundo de las fusiones, adquisiciones y mercados bursátiles. Dominar 'bail out' o 'write off' te dará una fluidez nativa en cualquier junta directiva.

parts.visual:
1. Bail out (Rescatar financieramente): 
- Proveer dinero a una empresa o país para salvarlo de la bancarrota. 
Ej: The government had to BAIL OUT the struggling banks during the crisis. 

2. Write off (Cancelar / Dar por perdido): 
- Cancelar una deuda que no se puede cobrar o depreciar un activo. 
Ej: The bank decided to WRITE OFF the $5 million loan as a bad debt. 

3. Cash in on (Sacar provecho de / Lucrarse): 
- Aprovechar una oportunidad, a menudo financiera, a veces de forma oportunista. 
Ej: Speculators tried to CASH IN ON the sudden surge in housing prices.
parts.audio: Welcome to Phrasal Verbs in High Finance. Number 1: Bail out. This means to provide financial rescue to a failing company or country. For example: The government had to BAIL OUT the struggling banks during the crisis. Number 2: Write off. To cancel a debt that will never be paid, or to depreciate an asset for tax purposes. For example: The bank decided to WRITE OFF the five million dollar loan as a bad debt. Number 3: Cash in on. To take advantage of a situation, especially financially. For example: Speculators tried to CASH IN ON the sudden surge in housing prices.

parts.visual:
4. Bottom out (Tocar fondo): 
- Llegar al punto más bajo antes de empezar a mejorar (usado en mercados/precios). 
Ej: Analysts believe the recession has finally BOTTOMED OUT. 

5. Claw back (Recuperar con esfuerzo / Restituir): 
- Recuperar dinero que ya se había pagado (como bonos a ejecutivos si cometen fraude). 
Ej: The board decided to CLAW BACK the CEO's bonuses after the accounting scandal. 

6. Prop up (Apuntalar / Sostener artificialmente): 
- Apoyar financiera o artificialmente algo que de otra manera caería. 
Ej: The central bank intervened to PROP UP the collapsing currency.
parts.audio: Number 4: Bottom out. To reach the lowest point before starting to rise again. Used a lot in stock markets. For example: Analysts believe the recession has finally BOTTOMED OUT. Number 5: Claw back. To legally recover money that has already been paid out, such as an executive bonus after a fraud discovery. For example: The board decided to CLAW BACK the CEO's bonuses after the accounting scandal. Number 6: Prop up. To support or sustain a failing economy, currency, or company artificially. For example: The central bank intervened to PROP UP the collapsing currency.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el phrasal verb financiero correcto.

questions.question: During the 2008 crisis, the US government had to ____ several major banks to prevent economic collapse. (Rescatar financieramente).
questions.explanation: Bail out = rescatar financieramente de la bancarrota.

questions.question: Since the debtor declared bankruptcy, the bank had to ____ the entire $10 million loan. (Dar por perdido / Cancelar).
questions.explanation: Write off = cancelar una deuda incobrable o deducir un gasto.

questions.question: Many pharmaceutical companies tried to ____ the pandemic by rapidly raising prices. (Sacar provecho de).
questions.explanation: Cash in on = lucrarse, sacar provecho de una situación.

questions.question: The stock market has been falling for months, but analysts hope prices will finally ____ next quarter. (Tocar fondo).
questions.explanation: Bottom out = tocar el punto más bajo antes de empezar a subir.

questions.question: The government is spending billions to ____ the struggling construction sector. (Apuntalar / Sostener).
questions.explanation: Prop up = apuntalar o sostener artificialmente algo que está cayendo.

questions.question: After the fraud was revealed, the shareholders demanded that the company ____ the bonuses paid to the executives. (Recuperar lo pagado).
questions.explanation: Claw back = recuperar dinero previamente otorgado (como bonos).

questions.question: The government provided a massive $50 billion ____ to save the airline industry. (Rescate - sustantivo).
questions.explanation: Bailout (como una sola palabra) es el sustantivo de 'bail out'.

questions.question: We can't recover that money, so we'll just have to write it ____ as a bad debt.
Influencers are quickly cashing ____ the new cryptocurrency trend.
The central bank intervened in the currency markets to prop ____ the national currency.
Property prices seem to have bottomed ____; we are starting to see a slight recovery.
The new legislation makes it easier for companies to claw ____ excessive executive pay.
A ____ is when investors sell off their shares rapidly because they fear a market crash. (Venta masiva).
questions.explanation: Sell-off = venta masiva de acciones que hace caer el precio.

questions.question: To avoid a hostile takeover, the board decided to buy ____ the aggressive shareholder. (Comprar su parte).
questions.explanation: Buy out = comprar la parte de alguien (o toda la empresa) para tomar el control.

questions.question: Inflation is eating ____ our profit margins. (Consumiendo/Erosionando).
questions.explanation: Eat into (profits / margins) = consumir o reducir gradualmente.

questions.question: The startup is burning ____ cash at an alarming rate. (Gastando rápidamente).
questions.explanation: Burn through (cash) = gastar dinero muy rápido.

questions.question: Our legal team managed to water ____ the strict regulations. (Diluir / Suavizar).
questions.explanation: Water down = diluir o hacer algo menos estricto o fuerte.

questions.question: The company was forced to lay ____ 20% of its workforce due to the recession. (Despedir).
questions.explanation: Lay off = despedir (por razones económicas, no por mal desempeño).

questions.question: We need to scale ____ production if we want to meet the global demand. (Aumentar a gran escala).
questions.explanation: Scale up = expandir o aumentar la producción o el tamaño de la empresa.

questions.question: The merger fell ____ at the last minute because of regulatory issues. (Fracasó / Se vino abajo).
questions.explanation: Fall through = fracasar, no concretarse (un trato o plan).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la preposición correcta del phrasal verb financiero.

questions.question: The government will bail ____ the banks. (Rescatar)
We must write ____ this debt. (Dar por perdida)
They want to cash in ____ the trend. (Lucrarse de)
The market finally bottomed ____. (Tocó fondo)
We will claw ____ the bonuses. (Recuperar lo pagado)
They intervened to prop ____ the currency. (Apuntalar)
Taxes are eating ____ our profits. (Erosionando/Consumiendo)
We are burning ____ cash. (Gastando rápido)
The deal fell ____. (Fracasó)
We need to scale ____ our operations. (Aumentar masivamente)

stages.title: Listening Comprehension
stages.description: Escucha y selecciona la frase financiera correcta.

questions.question: Listen carefully.
Listen carefully.
questions.tts_text: We have to write off the debt.
options: We have to write off the debt.
They have to write off the debt.
We had to write off the debt.
We have to write out the debt.
questions.correct_answer: We have to write off the debt.

questions.question: Listen carefully.
questions.tts_text: They are cashing in on the trend.
options: They are cashing in on the trend.
We are cashing in on the trend.
They were cashing in on the trend.
They are cashing out on the trend.
questions.correct_answer: They are cashing in on the trend.

questions.question: Listen carefully.
Listen carefully.
questions.tts_text: We will claw back the money.
options: We will claw back the money.
They will claw back the money.
I will claw back the money.
We would claw back the money.
questions.correct_answer: We will claw back the money.

questions.question: Listen carefully.
questions.tts_text: They are trying to prop up the bank.
options: They are trying to prop up the bank.
We are trying to prop up the bank.
They are trying to prop out the bank.
They were trying to prop up the bank.
questions.correct_answer: They are trying to prop up the bank.

questions.question: Listen carefully.
questions.tts_text: Taxes are eating into our margins.
options: Taxes are eating into our margins.
Taxes are eating into your margins.
Taxes were eating into our margins.
Taxes are eating up our margins.
questions.correct_answer: Taxes are eating into our margins.

questions.question: Listen carefully.
Listen carefully.
Listen carefully.
questions.tts_text: We need to scale up rapidly.
options: We need to scale up rapidly.
They need to scale up rapidly.
We needed to scale up rapidly.
We need to scale out rapidly.
questions.correct_answer: We need to scale up rapidly.
